Definition: a sour grape (as sharp in taste)
BiblicalUsage: Chartsan is a sour grape, the husk, and it appears once, in the law of the Nazarite: all the days of his separation he shall eat nothing that is made of the vine tree, from the kernels even to the husk.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the verse shows how thorough consecration is: not even the husk of a grape is allowed.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
